'''Aaron Jamal Brooks''' (born January 14, 1985) is an American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player. He was selected 26th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. Brooks won the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] for the 2009–10 season.

==High school career==
Brooks, a high-profile recruit out of [[Franklin High School (Seattle, Washington)|Franklin High School]] in Seattle, "earned just about every honor possible" while leading his team to the Washington 4A State Championship as a senior.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Crow |first=Robert |date=March 15, 2003 |title=Brooks leads Franklin Quakers to 4A state title |url=https://www.seattlepi.com/news/article/brooks-leads-franklin-quakers-to-4a-state-title-1109856.php |access-date=August 22, 2024 |website=seattlepi.com}}</ref> As a high school senior he averaged 24.3 points, 7.0 assists, 3.3 rebounds and 2.3 steals per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aaron Brooks - Men's Basketball |url=https://goducks.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/aaron-brooks/3514 |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=University of Oregon Athletics |language=en}}</ref> In that championship game, Brooks went head-to-head with future [[Gonzaga Bulldogs|Gonzaga Bulldog]] and two-time NBA champion [[Adam Morrison]]. Brooks finished with 38 points in the 67–55 win. Morrison finished with 37 in the loss, but was still named Tournament MVP after matching the then four-game scoring title.<ref name=":0" />

Considered a four-star recruit by [[247Sports.com]], Brooks was listed as the No. 4 point guard and the No. 30 player in the nation in 2003.<ref>[https://247sports.com/Player/Aaron-Brooks-68106/?Institution=22578 Aaron Brooks Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Brooks played his [[college basketball|college]] career at the [[University of Oregon]] in 2007. He was a four-year starter for the [[Oregon Ducks|Ducks]], and finished his career with 13.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game. In his first year at Oregon, Brooks took over the starting point guard role previously occupied by guard [[Luke Ridnour]], who went on to play in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. Despite missing 10 games with a broken bone in his wrist, Brooks earned [[Pac-10]] All-Freshman honors. Brooks was named honorable mention all-[[Pac-10]] for his efforts as a sophomore, a season which included a 34-point effort against [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]]. After a disappointing junior year at Oregon culminating in a suspension during a game against Washington, Brooks rebounded to become one of the leading candidates for Pac-10 Player of the Year. He led the Ducks to a number of key victories, including game winners over then #1 ranked [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and then #10 [[Arizona Wildcats basketball|Arizona]] in [[Tucson, Arizona|Tucson]]. Brooks scored a team high 31 points and grabbed 8 rebounds in an overtime road win against then top 25 ranked [[Washington State Cougars|Washington State]], helping to hand the Cougars their first home loss of the 2006–07 season. At the half-way mark of Pac-10 conference play, Brooks was averaging 19.1 points and 4.5 assists per game in leading Oregon to a top 10 ranking and a 19–2 overall record. The Ducks went on to finish and tie for third place in the Pac-10 conference, and won the Pac-10 Championship tournament following an impressive three-day run over Arizona, [[University of California, Berkeley|Cal]] and USC. Oregon advanced to the Midwest Regional Final where they lost to defending champion [[2006–07 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]]. Brooks was announced as one of 22 finalists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]], which is given to the top college basketball player in the nation. Brooks was one of 10 players named to the Wooden All-American Team, and he was also [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]]. He won the men's three point shootout on March 29, 2007, to finish off his NCAA career, but lost the "battle of the sexes" to [[Katie Gearlds]] of [[Purdue University]]. He graduated from Oregon in 2007 with a degree in political science.

==Professional career==

===Houston Rockets (2007–2011)===
On June 28, 2007, Brooks was taken 26th overall in the first round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]]. During the 2007–08 season, he spent time with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].

On February 19, 2009, [[Rafer Alston]], the Rockets' starting point guard at the time, was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] minutes before the trading deadline, making way for Brooks to become the starter. As a starter, he averaged around 14.0 points and 4.5 assists per game. On April 21, 2009, Brooks scored 11 points in 27 seconds in a first round 107–103 playoff loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], in which Brooks played a huge part in Houston's rally, scoring three 3-pointers and a fast break lay-up. While the Rockets lost that game, they were able to eliminate Portland in six games. Brooks scored a then career-high 34 points in Game 4 of the [[2009 NBA Playoffs|2009 Western Conference semi-finals]] as the Rockets, without [[Yao Ming]], defeated the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] to even the series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=290510010|date=May 10, 2009|work=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=December 12, 2009|title= Los Angeles Lakers vs. Houston Rockets Box Score}}</ref> However, the Lakers eventually won the series in 7 games as well as the championship.

On January 13, 2010, Brooks scored a new career high of 43 points in a triple overtime win against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|work=[[ESPN]].com|access-date=January 11, 2010|date=January 11, 2010|title=Houston Rockets vs. Minnesota Timberwolves|agency=Associated Press|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300113010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100119034152/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300113010|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2010}}</ref> On March 15, 2010, Brooks scored the game winning shot against the Denver Nuggets with 2.9 seconds left in the game. On March 17, 2010, Brooks shot 7–7 from behind the three arc against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], setting a new franchise record. On April 11, 2010, Brooks became only the sixth player in NBA history to make over 200 3-pointers and over 400 assists in a single season.

On April 23, 2010, he was named [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]], averaging 19.6 points, 5.3 assists, and 2.6 rebounds per game.

On November 6, 2010, Brooks suffered a sprained ankle. He returned on December 19, 2010, in a 102–93 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]], in which he came off the bench for 15 minutes and recorded 9 points (all 3-pointers). In his first start since return from his injury, on January 10, 2011, he tied his season-high 24 points, in a win over the [[Boston Celtics]].

===Phoenix Suns (2011)===
On February 24, 2011, Brooks was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Goran Dragić]] and a first-round pick the team got from the [[Orlando Magic]] in an earlier trade.

===Guangdong Southern Tigers (2011–2012)===
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Brooks signed to play for the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns guard Aaron Brooks plans to sign with Chinese team |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/phoenix-suns-guard-aaron/ |access-date=2024-08-22 |website=www.sportsnet.ca |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sports.163.com/11/1118/09/7J4QD0KH00052UUC.html |title=布鲁克斯:合同摆在面前很难拒绝 下周将飞广东 |access-date=2011-11-18 |archive-date=2016-03-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304130745/http://sports.163.com/11/1118/09/7J4QD0KH00052UUC.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 6, 2012, Brooks scored 40 points while playing 38 minutes off the bench as Guangdong defeated the [[Tianjin Ronggang]] 110–97. Brooks was 5 points shy of tying the Guangdong points scored record made by former player [[Du Feng]]. On February 16, 2012, Brooks was selected as the replacement starting point guard for the 2012 [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] All-Star game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.163.com/12/0216/11/7QCPD6TD00052UUC.html|title=Cba全明星赛大名单出炉 老马大郅分任星锐队主帅|date=16 February 2012|access-date=18 February 2012|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304120408/http://sports.163.com/12/0216/11/7QCPD6TD00052UUC.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The original starter, [[J.R. Smith]], decided not to play for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sports.163.com/12/0211/13/7Q034I8H00052UUC.html|title=Jr确定不参加Cba全明星 常规赛结束后将返回美国|date=11 February 2012|access-date=18 February 2012|archive-date=14 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114083736/http://sports.163.com/12/0211/13/7Q034I8H00052UUC.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Brooks was also selected to participate for the CBA's Three-Point Shootout competition. In the three-point shootout, Brooks was one point shy from entering the final round of the competition. In the All-Star game, Brooks led all competitors with 9 assists, but his Northern All-Stars team lost to the Southern All-Stars, 122–112. On March 8, the [[NBA on TNT]] did a segment on Brooks' time in China with Guangdong. Brooks led the team in assists for each game leading up to the [[2012 CBA Playoffs|2012 CBA Finals]], where they lost to the [[Stephon Marbury]]-led [[Beijing Ducks]].

===Sacramento Kings (2012–2013)===
After an absence from the NBA during the 2011–12 season, the Suns initially extended a qualifying offer to Brooks for the 2012–13 season,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2012/news/06/28/suns-offers.ap/ Suns extend qualifying offers to Lopez, Brooks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222125641/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/06/28/suns-offers.ap/ |date=2016-02-22 }}</ref> but would later withdraw the offer,<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/07/brooks-suns.ap/ Suns withdraw qualifying offer to guard Brooks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024103950/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/07/07/brooks-suns.ap/ |date=2015-10-24 }}</ref> thus making Brooks an unrestricted free agent. Three teams that expressed interest in him were the [[Dallas Mavericks]], the [[Sacramento Kings]], and Brooks' former team, the [[Houston Rockets]]. In July 2012, Brooks signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 22, 2012|date=July 16, 2012|title=KINGS AND AARON BROOKS AGREE ON A CONTRACT IN PRINCIPLE|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-and-aaron-brooks-agree-principle-contract}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 17, 2013|date=July 16, 2012|title=Kings sign point guard Aaron Brooks|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8171794/sacramento-kings-sign-guard-aaron-brooks-waive-hassan-whiteside}}</ref> He was waived by the Kings on March 1, 2013.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-waive-aaron-brooks KINGS WAIVE AARON BROOKS]</ref>

===Return to Houston (2013–2014)===
He later signed with the Rockets on March 5, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 5, 2013|date=March 5, 2013|title= He's Back – Rockets Sign Free Agent Aaron Brooks|url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/hes-back-rockets-sign-free-agent-aaron-brooks}}</ref> On June 30, 2013, he was waived by the Rockets,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13620 |title=Houston Rockets waive Aaron Brooks and Carlos Delfino |access-date=2013-07-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130827213233/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13620 |archive-date=2013-08-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but on July 19, 2013, he rejoined the team, reaching an agreement on a one-year minimum contract.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13833 |title=Houston Rockets re-sign Aaron Brooks, sign Reggie Williams |access-date=2013-07-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130723014751/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13833 |archive-date=2013-07-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2014)===
On February 20, 2014, Brooks was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Jordan Hamilton (basketball)|Jordan Hamilton]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 20, 2014|date=July 14, 2015|title=Denver Nuggets Acquire G Aaron Brooks From Houston|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-acquire-g-aaron-brooks-houston}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2014–2016)===
On July 22, 2014, Brooks signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 23, 2014|date=July 22, 2014|title=Bulls sign free agent guard Aaron Brooks|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agent-guard-aaron-brooks}}</ref>

On July 14, 2015, Brooks re-signed with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bulls sign Aaron Brooks|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/official-bulls-sign-aaron-brooks|access-date=July 14, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2016–2017)===
[[File:Kyle Korver (February 15, 2017).jpg|thumb|right|Brooks defends a shot by [[Kyle Korver]] during a 2017 game]]
On July 21, 2016, Brooks signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-aaron-brooks|title=Pacers Sign Aaron Brooks|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2016|access-date=July 21, 2016}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2017–2018)===
On September 21, 2017, Brooks signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-aaron-brooks|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN AARON BROOKS|work=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2017|access-date=September 24, 2017}}</ref>

===Illawarra Hawks (2019)===
On June 20, 2019, Brooks signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] in Australia for the [[2019–20 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/hawks-sign-former-nba-guard-aaron-brooks|title=Hawks Sign Former NBA Guard Aaron Brooks|work=NBL.com.au|date=June 20, 2019|access-date=June 20, 2019|archive-date=July 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712174337/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/hawks-sign-former-nba-guard-aaron-brooks|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 28, 2019, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after tearing his left Achilles tendon in a game the previous day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/aaron-brooks-ruled-out-for-the-rest-of-the-season|title=Aaron Brooks Ruled Out For The Rest of the Season|work=NBL.com.au|date=October 28, 2019|access-date=October 28, 2019|archive-date=October 28, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191028052537/https://nbl.com.au/news/aaron-brooks-ruled-out-for-the-rest-of-the-season|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On November 25, 2020, Brooks joined the [[New York Knicks]] as a two-way liaison.<ref>{{cite web |title=Knicks Announce Staff Hirings |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-announce-staff-hirings |website=New York Knicks |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> His primary role will be coaching Knicks players who are on [[two-way contract]]s.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Berman |first1=Marc |title=Knicks hire Aaron Brooks for unusual coaching role |url=https://nypost.com/2020/11/25/knicks-add-aaron-brooks-to-staff-as-two-way-liason/ |website=New York Post |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 25, 2020}}</ref> Brooks is serving under head coach [[Tom Thibodeau]], whom he played for at stints in both Chicago and Minnesota.
